Example Analyses

Michael Hunt

16/05/2024

This notebook uses the penguin data set from the palmerpenguins package to illustrate the use of correlation, linear regression and t-test / Wilcox tests in R.

library(tidyverse)
## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
## ✔ dplyr     1.1.4     ✔ readr     2.1.5
## ✔ forcats   1.0.0     ✔ stringr   1.5.1
## ✔ ggplot2   3.5.1     ✔ tibble    3.2.1
## ✔ lubridate 1.9.3     ✔ tidyr     1.3.1
## ✔ purrr     1.0.2     
## ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
## ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()

## $ island            <fct> Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgerse…
## $ bill_length_mm    <dbl> 39.1, 39.5, 40.3, NA, 36.7, 39.3, 38.9, 39.2, 34.1, …
## $ bill_depth_mm     <dbl> 18.7, 17.4, 18.0, NA, 19.3, 20.6, 17.8, 19.6, 18.1, …
## $ flipper_length_mm <int> 181, 186, 195, NA, 193, 190, 181, 195, 193, 190, 186…
## $ body_mass_g       <int> 3750, 3800, 3250, NA, 3450, 3650, 3625, 4675, 3475, …

Correlation

adelie %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs( x = "Bill length (mm)",
        y = "Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_cowplot()
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

bill_length<-adelie$bill_length_mm
bill_depth<-adelie$bill_depth_mm

cor.test(bill_length, bill_depth, method = "pearson")
## 
##  Pearson's product-moment correlation
## 
## data:  bill_length and bill_depth
## t = 5.1933, df = 149, p-value = 6.674e-07
## alternative hypothesis: true correlation is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.2472226 0.5187796
## sample estimates:
##       cor 
## 0.3914917

Simple linear regression

bill.model<-lm(bill_depth ~ bill_length, data = adelie)
anova(bill.model)
summary(bill.model)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = bill_depth ~ bill_length, data = adelie)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.1512 -0.8012 -0.0698  0.5766  3.5032 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) 11.40912    1.33893   8.521 1.61e-14 ***
## bill_length  0.17883    0.03444   5.193 6.67e-07 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.123 on 149 degrees of freedom
##   (1 observation deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.1533, Adjusted R-squared:  0.1476 
## F-statistic: 26.97 on 1 and 149 DF,  p-value: 6.674e-07
adelie %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs( x = "Bill length (mm)",
        y = "Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_line(color = "#8ccde3",
                                  linetype = 2,
                                  linewidth=0.5))
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

adelie %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs( x = "Bill length (mm)",
        y = "Bill depth (mm)") +

t-test / Wilcox tests for difference

penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=species,y=body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x= " Species",
       y = "Body mass (g)") +
  theme_cowplot()
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

penguins %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=body_mass_g)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(x= " Body mass (g)",
       y = "Count") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 1) +
  theme_cowplot()
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_bin()`).

test for normality

penguins %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  shapiro_test(body_mass_g)

t_test / Wilcox test

adelie_bodymass <- penguins %>% filter(species == "Adelie") %>% select(body_mass_g) %>% pull()
chinstrap_bodymass <- penguins %>% filter(species == "Chinstrap") %>% select(body_mass_g) %>% pull()
gentoo_bodymass <- penguins %>% filter(species == "Gentoo") %>% select(body_mass_g) %>% pull()

Do Adelie penguin body masses differ from those of Chinstrap penguins?

t.test(adelie_bodymass,chinstrap_bodymass)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  adelie_bodymass and chinstrap_bodymass
## t = -0.54309, df = 152.45, p-value = 0.5879
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -150.38481   85.53284
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
##  3700.662  3733.088
wilcox.test(adelie_bodymass,chinstrap_bodymass)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  adelie_bodymass and chinstrap_bodymass
## W = 4831, p-value = 0.4855
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

Do Chinstrap penguin body masses differ from those of Gentoo penguins?

t.test(chinstrap_bodymass,gentoo_bodymass)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  chinstrap_bodymass and gentoo_bodymass
## t = -20.628, df = 170.4, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -1471.440 -1214.416
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
##  3733.088  5076.016
